sections.h2: Who collects property tax in the Town of Greenburgh?
sections.html:
The Greenburgh Receiver of Taxes, based in Town Hall at 177 Hillside Avenue, collects for Westchester County, the town, the fire districts and the ten school districts inside Greenburgh. The Tax Department's page calls it the largest municipal collection agency in Westchester and says it brings in over a quarter billion dollars a year. The receiver listed on the town's staff directory is Venita A. Howard, and the department's phone is 914-989-1550.

The office is open Monday through Friday, 9 am to 5 pm, and stays open until 7 pm on the last day of each collection period (April 30, September 30 and January 31). Checks go to Greenburgh Receiver Of Taxes with the account number written on them. In person the office takes checks and exact-change cash under $10,000, and the lobby has a mailbox where checks, never cash, can be dropped.

Online payment is at the town's municipal tax payments portal. Bank ACH payments carry no fee, and card payments carry a variable rate. Liens cannot be paid online, so anyone with a lien calls or visits the Tax Office.

sections.h2: When are Greenburgh property taxes due?
sections.html:
Greenburgh collects in three windows, and the Tax Department identifies their last days as April 30, September 30 and January 31. The Part 1 school tax for 2026 was due September 30, with bills mailed August 31, so that date has passed. The next last day on the office's own list is January 31.

  • Village taxes are not collected by the town. Residents of a village contact their Village Hall for those due dates.
  • Mail counts by postmark from the USPS, FedEx, UPS or DHL. Pitney Bowes meter stamps and foreign postmarks are not accepted.
  • Payments sent through a bank's online bill pay service carry no US postmark, so the town treats the date it receives them as the payment date.
  • Since December 24, 2025, the USPS machine postmark reflects the date mail is first processed at a regional facility, so a letter dropped in a local box near a deadline can show a later date.

The town page also cites two state rules. Real Property Tax Law section 922 says that a bill that was never mailed or never received does not affect the validity of the tax or interest. Section 920 says the Tax Receiver has no authority to waive penalties for any reason.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Greenburgh assessment?
sections.html:
Greenburgh runs two tracks: a short informal online review in spring and a formal grievance in June. The town's assessment page says the assessment should reflect market value as of July 1 of the previous year. Property record cards and a sales map are on the town's Axis GIS site, which is where owners gather comparable sales.

The informal review ran May 15 to June 11 in 2026. You fill in a portal form with proof of overassessment, and a town appraiser answers within 72 hours. If you agree to a reduction you sign a stipulation and the matter ends for the year. Owners who already met with assessment staff about that year's value must go straight to the formal grievance.

The formal grievance uses form RP-524 and runs from June 1 until 9 pm on the third Tuesday in June, which was June 16 in 2026. Postmarked-only filings are treated as late. You do not need an attorney. After the final roll on September 15, the Board of Assessment Review mails its results, and an owner has until October 15 to file a small claims assessment review with Westchester County. A reduction first shows up on the Town and County tax bill the following April. The Assessment Department's number is 914-989-1520.

sections.h2: What is Greenburgh like for a homeowner?
sections.html:
Greenburgh is a town in western Westchester County with 36.1 square miles, bordered by the Hudson River on the west, Yonkers on the south, Mount Pleasant on the north, and White Plains and Scarsdale on the east. About half the population lives in its six incorporated villages, and the rest live in the unincorporated area, which includes the Fairview, Greenville and Hartsdale census-designated places plus East Irvington, North Elmsford and South Ardsley.

The Thruway (I-87), the Cross Westchester Expressway, the Saw Mill River Parkway, the Bronx River Parkway and the Sprain Brook Parkway all cross the town. Metro-North's Hudson Line stops at Hastings-on-Hudson, Dobbs Ferry, Ardsley-on-Hudson, Irvington and Tarrytown, and the Harlem Line stops at Hartsdale. The Westchester Library System has its headquarters in Elmsford. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts figures below show what that location means for housing.

sections.h2: Which STAR benefit applies to a Greenburgh school tax bill?
sections.html:
The state offers Basic STAR to owner-occupied primary residences and Enhanced STAR to owners aged 65 and over, and both affect only school district tax. Basic STAR is based on the first $30,000 of a home's full value, with an income limit of $500,000 for the credit. Enhanced STAR requires household income of $110,750 or less for the 2026-2027 school year.

Since Greenburgh has ten school districts, the dollar savings depend on which district serves the parcel. The Tax Department publishes a 2026-2027 STAR school tax savings sheet and a projected tax sheet for an average household. Registration for the credit goes through the state's Tax Department rather than the town.

sections.h2: How should I handle a tax payoff before selling in Greenburgh?
sections.html:
Start with the Tax Office. Its page tells new owners and anyone who recently satisfied a mortgage to call 914-989-1550, and it tells anyone who receives a bill for a property they no longer own to say so. Homeowners with escrowed taxes get a copy of the bill from the Receiver twice a year, so a lender may have paid the current installments already.

  1. Ask the Tax Office which installments are open and whether any lien exists on the account.
  2. Request the figure for any lien directly, since liens are handled in person or by phone and not on the online portal.
  3. Give the payoff numbers to the closing attorney.
  4. Confirm with the buyer's side which village, if any, bills separately.

Town and County tax is billed on a calendar that closes April 30, school tax closes September 30 and January 31, and village tax runs on its own schedule. A closing between those dates needs the current status in writing from each office that bills the parcel.

faqs.q: What are the last collection days for Greenburgh taxes?
faqs.a: April 30, September 30 and January 31, according to the Tax Department's hours listing. The office stays open until 7 pm on those dates. Village taxes follow separate dates set by each Village Hall.

faqs.q: Can the Greenburgh Receiver of Taxes waive a late penalty?
faqs.a: No. The town page cites Real Property Tax Law section 920, which says the Receiver has no authority to waive penalties on real estate taxes. Section 922 adds that a bill that was not mailed or not received does not change the tax or interest.

faqs.q: Can I pay a Greenburgh tax lien online?
faqs.a: No. The Tax Department states that liens cannot be paid online. Call the Tax Office at 914-989-1550 or visit 177 Hillside Avenue to get the amount and pay it.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in Greenburgh?
faqs.a: The third Tuesday in June, which was June 16 in 2026. Applications on form RP-524 are accepted from June 1 until 9 pm that day. A late or postmark-only application is not reviewed.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for small claims assessment review after Greenburgh's final roll?
faqs.a: October 15. The final roll is filed September 15, grievance results are mailed then, and an owner who disagrees has 30 days to file with Westchester County.
